newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks firmer in active Monday trade.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks firmer in active Monday trade.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares opened the week firmer in active trade with brokers saying the market debut on Monday of agro-industrial concern CFI Holdings seemed to have revived confidence in the market.
The industrial index rose 39.04 points to push back though the 10,300 level, closing at 10,300.67.
CFI Holdings closed at 210 cents bid with sellers at 220 cents and deals at 215 in heavy volume.
"We saw CFI opening very strongly and it must have put some confidence back into the market," one broker said.
"Buyers seem to be coming back but the focus is still on new issues. CFI is now out of the way and everyone is now looking at Randalls," he added.
Manufacturing, construction and distribution company Randalls opened its new issue last Monday. It is looking to raise Z$65 million through the issue of 50 million shares at 130 cents each.

On the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange on Monday, blue-chip hotels and beverages conglomerate Delta gained 10 cents to 1,700, publishers Zimpapers leapt 400 cents to 4,200, hotel and supermarket group Meikles rose 50 cents to 2,650 while sugar refinery ZSR added 25 cents to 1,425.

Against the trend, timber producer Border dropped 100 cents to 950, Alloys cut 25 cents to 600, construction firm J and F and winery Afdis lost 20 cents each to 430 and 470 respectively while glass firm PGI shed 10 cents to 630.
Minings were quiet with Wankie Colliery unchanged while Falgold slipped two cents to 75 and Rio Tinto dropped 50 cents to 2,300.
The mining index lost 5.82 points to close at 993.24.
